name: 8.3 Probability Distribution Needed for Hypothesis Testing
_note: Built 2026-08-12. Two reuses (q16-full-ht-one-mean-fresh, q8-ht-one-proportion - both health=ok, never filed) plus eight authored (q32-which-distribution, q33-sigma-known-vs-unknown, q34-test-conditions, q35-np-nq-check, q36-proportion-condition-failure, q37-binomial-vs-normal, q38-mean-or-proportion, pre-frq-grade-a-distribution-selection) = ten. Points 10+10+10+10+10+10+10+9+9+12 = 100. BookSHelf 8.3 is the probability distribution needed for hypothesis testing: matching a test to its distribution (Table 8.3.1), the two questions that make the choice (mean or proportion? then is sigma known?), the assumptions each test requires, and the np > 5 / nq > 5 condition. Pre-FRQ is authored-first (no distribution-selection FRQ exists anywhere in questions/frq/): categories Name the Distribution (3) / State the Deciding Facts (4) / Check the Conditions (3), dropped category CHECK THE CONDITIONS (a plausible answer names the distribution and the deciding facts without ever verifying the assumptions).

questions.title: Full HT for One Mean (Fresh Context) - Compute t-statistic, df, p-value, decision at alpha for a one-mean test with a randomized story context
Full hypothesis test for one population proportion (p-value approach) with randomized story contexts
Which Distribution - the curve the test runs on, and the deciding fact that chose it
Sigma Known vs Unknown - which spread you were given, and the distribution that follows
Test Conditions - the requirement at risk in the scenario, whether it is met, and why the condition exists
The np and nq Check - n*p0 and n*(1-p0) under the null, and whether the normal approximation is allowed
Proportion Condition Failure - why the normal approximation cannot be used, and what the correct approach is
Binomial vs Normal - what the raw count follows, and when it may be treated as normal
Mean or Proportion - the parameter from the claim, and which row of Table 8.3.1 the test lives in
